sources.entry: OpenSMTPD - Secure SMTP server implementation from the OpenBSD project. (Source Code) ISC C/deb

summary.one_liner: OpenSMTPD is a free, server-side SMTP mail transfer agent from the OpenBSD project that implements RFC 5321 plus some standard extensions.
summary.what_it_does: OpenSMTPD implements the server side of the SMTP protocol (RFC 5321) with some additional standard extensions, letting a machine send and receive email with other SMTP systems. The README says it runs on Linux, FreeBSD, OpenBSD, NetBSD, DragonFlyBSD and macOS. It is installed either from distribution packages (apt, apk, yum, zypper, MacPorts) or built from source with configure and make. Its single control utility, smtpctl, can run in compatibility mode under historical names such as sendmail, newaliases, mailq and makemap, if the system links them to it. Configuration lives in /etc/smtpd.conf, and the daemon is started with smtpd, with a -dv flag for debug and verbose output. The README recommends running two dedicated users (_smtpd and _smtpq) for better security.
use_cases: receive and send email over SMTP
relay mail on BSD or Linux servers
provide a sendmail-style interface for local mail submission
how_to_run: sudo apt install opensmtpd (Debian/Ubuntu; other distributions listed in README)
git clone the repository, or download a release tarball
Create the _smtpd and _smtpq users as described in the README, and configure /etc/smtpd.conf
smtpd (or smtpd -dv for debug and verbose mode)
stack: autoconf, automake, bison or byacc, libtool (git builds only)
notable: Comes from the OpenBSD project and is available as a package on many Unix-like systems
Single smtpctl binary that can act as sendmail, newaliases, mailq and makemap through compatibility links
Privilege separation via two dedicated system users (_smtpd and _smtpq)
Packaged in many distributions, and the README notes some distributions backport security fixes
caveats: The README warns the repository may lag behind the OpenBSD smtpd source, so downstream maintainers should check backported security fixes
Some distributions ship old versions of OpenSMTPD
Building from source needs several dependencies, and macOS needs a newer bison and a libevent path passed to configure
